title: Shopping & money
goal: Ask prices, bargain politely, buy clothes in the right size, and point out 'this one' and 'that one'.
intro: Tamil has a beautifully regular system of **demonstratives** built on three initial vowels: **இ-** 'this, here' (near me), **அ-** 'that, there' (away from me) and **எ-** 'which, where' (question). Once you know this, இது/அது/எது, இங்க/அங்க/எங்க, இப்போ/அப்போ/எப்போ all fall into place.

vocab.note: spoken: சீப் chīp; expensive = விலை அதிகம் / காஸ்ட்லி
spoken: விக்கு vikku; present விக்கிறாங்க vikkirānga
spoken: குடு kuḍu; past குடுத்தேன் kuḍuttēn

phrases.en: Do you have this in a bigger size?

grammar.title: The இ / அ / எ system: this, that, which
grammar.body:
Tamil demonstratives are built on three vowels: **இ-** near the speaker, **அ-** away from the speaker, **எ-** question.

இது *idu* this · அது *adu* that · எது *edu* which (one)?
இந்த *inda* this… · அந்த *anda* that… · எந்த *enda* which…?
இங்க *inga* here · அங்க *anga* there · எங்க *enga* where?
இப்போ *ippō* now · அப்போ *appō* then · எப்போ *eppō* when?
இப்படி *ippaḍi* like this · அப்படி *appaḍi* like that · எப்படி *eppaḍi* how?
இவ்வளவு *ivvaḷavu* this much · அவ்வளவு · எவ்வளவு how much?
இவரு / அவரு — this / that person (respectful)

**இது/அது** stand alone ('this one'); **இந்த/அந்த** go before a noun ('this shirt'). After இந்த/அந்த a following hard consonant is doubled in writing: அந்தச் சட்டை (when writing casual speech, people often leave it out, especially before ச: அந்த சட்டை).

examples.en: I want this one, not that one.
Which shop did you buy it from?
I don't have that much money.

grammar.title: The object: accusative -ஐ (spoken -அ)
grammar.body:
When a **specific, definite** thing is the object of a verb, it takes the accusative **-ஐ** *-ai* (spoken often **-அ** *-a*): அந்தச் சட்டையைக் காட்டுங்க 'show me that shirt'. Indefinite or generic objects usually take no ending: நான் சட்டை வாங்கணும் 'I need to buy a shirt'.

Pronouns: என்னை / என்ன *ennai* 'me', உங்களை / உங்கள *ungaḷai* 'you', அவரை 'him/her', இதை / இத 'this', அதை / அத 'that'. Nouns use the oblique stem: வீடு → வீட்டை, மரம் → மரத்தை.

The emphatic **-ஏ** *-ē* means 'this very one, the same': இதையே 'this very one'.

examples.en: Where did you buy that sari?

dialogue.title: Bargaining for a shirt
dialogue.setting: Tom shops for a shirt at a street stall on Ranganathan Street.

lines.speaker: Seller
lines.en: Come in, sir! What do you need?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.en: Show me that blue shirt, please.

lines.speaker: Seller
lines.native: இதுவா? சூப்பர் காட்டன் சார். என்ன சைஸ்?
lines.roman: iduvā? sūppar kāṭṭan sār. enna sais?
lines.en: This one? Superb cotton, sir. What size?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.native: அறுநூறா? ரொம்ப அதிகம். முன்னூறு ரூபா தர்றேன்.
lines.roman: arunūrā? romba adigam. munnūru rūbā tarrēn.
lines.en: Six hundred? That's a lot. I'll give three hundred.

lines.speaker: Seller
lines.en: Oh sir, that won't work! Give me five hundred.

lines.speaker: Seller
lines.en: OK sir, for you, four hundred and fifty.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.en: OK, I'll take this one. Can I pay by GPay?

lines.speaker: Seller
lines.en: Go ahead, sir. Thanks, come again!

culture: Bargaining is expected at street stalls and markets but not in fixed-price shops, supermarkets or malls. Stay friendly and smiling — it's a social game, not a fight. Digital payments (UPI apps like GPay and PhonePe) are now used everywhere, even at tiny tea stalls. Tamil Nadu is famous for Kanchipuram silk saris (காஞ்சிப் பட்டு), the most prized wedding saris.

tip.title: Prices and rupees
tip.body:
- Ask the price with **என்ன விலை?** 'what price?' or **எவ்வளவு?** 'how much?'.
- Rupees: written ரூபாய், said **ரூபா**: நூறு ரூபா.
- 'Per kilo' needs no extra word: **கிலோ** அம்பது ரூபா 'fifty rupees a kilo'.
- **காசு** is the everyday word for money; **பணம்** is a little more formal.
tip.pattern: thing + என்ன விலை?  ·  கிலோ + price + ரூபா

sentences.en: How much is rice a kilo?
Fifty rupees a kilo.
Half a kilo, please.
How much is the milk?
How many rupees altogether?
I don't have any money on me right now.
Do you have change for a hundred rupees?
No change? Never mind.
I'll give you the money later.

tip.title: இ- here, அ- there, எ- which?
tip.body:
- Before a noun: **இந்த** 'this', **அந்த** 'that', **எந்த** 'which': அந்த சட்டை.
- On their own: **இது** 'this one', **அது** 'that one', **எது** 'which one?'.
- The same vowels run through the language: இங்க / அங்க / எங்க, இவ்வளவு / அவ்வளவு / எவ்வளவு.
- Don't put இது before a noun: it's **இந்த** சட்டை.
tip.pattern: இந்த / அந்த / எந்த + noun  ·  இது / அது / எது alone

sentences.en: How much is this shirt?
How much is that blue sari?
Not this one, give me that one.
Which colour do you like?
Which one looks good?
That shop has good saris.
Come here, look over this side.
Is this much enough?
Show me a different shirt, please.

tip.title: The thing you mean: -ஐ
tip.body:
- A **specific** thing you act on takes **-ஐ**: அந்த சட்டை → அந்த சட்டை**யை**க் காட்டுங்க 'show me that shirt'.
- 'A shirt, any shirt' takes nothing: ஒரு சட்டை வாங்கணும்.
- இது → **இதை**, அது → **அதை**; நான் → **என்னை**.
- In fast speech -ஐ often sounds like -அ: சட்டைய.

sentences.en: Show me that veshti, please.
Can I try on these sandals?
Try that shirt on.

sentences.native: இந்த துணியைப் பாருங்க, ரொம்ப நல்லா இருக்கு.
sentences.roman: inda tuṇiyaip pārunga, romba nallā irukku.
sentences.en: Look at this cloth, it's really good.
Give me those black sandals, please.
We could buy this sari for Mum.
Put that here, please.
I need to buy a pair of trousers.
I don't know my size.
This size is too small.

tip.title: How to haggle
tip.body:
- At markets and small shops bargaining is normal; in big stores and malls prices are fixed.
- Start with **ரொம்ப விலை அதிகம்** 'that's too expensive', then **கொஞ்சம் குறைங்க** 'bring it down a bit'.
- Ask for the bottom line: **கடைசியா என்ன விலை?**
- Agree with **இதையே எடுத்துக்கிறேன்**: the **-ஏ** means 'this very one'.

sentences.en: Bring it down a bit, brother.
Is there a discount?
Everything is cheap in this shop.
Can you bargain here?
Will you give it to me for three hundred rupees?
This is the final price.
The shopkeeper brought the price down.
Give me that same red shirt.
OK, four hundred rupees. I'll take it.

tip.title: Can I…? with -லாமா
tip.body:
- Verb + **-லாமா?** asks 'can I / may I / shall we?': **பண்ணலாமா?**, **போட்டுப் பாக்கலாமா?**
- Most shops take phone payments: **ஜிபே பண்ணலாமா?** 'can I pay by GPay?'.
- Cards: **கார்டு எடுப்பீங்களா?** 'do you take cards?'.
- Ask for a receipt with **பில் குடுங்க** or **ரசீது குடுங்க**.

sentences.en: What does the bill come to?
Can I pay by card?
Do you take GPay here?
A receipt, please.
I gave you five hundred rupees.
Give me the change later.
Do they sell vegetables in this shop?
He sells old books.
I don't have cash, I'll pay by GPay.
